thema_eingabe: Meta's AI support bot handed hackers 20,000 Instagram accounts

skript.thema: Meta's AI support bot handed hackers Instagram accounts

teile.name: Hook
teile.text: Hackers now reset Instagram passwords by simply asking Meta's AI nicely. Meta's AI assistant did it, no malware needed. How?
teile.szene: Painted open-world-game poster style: the black-haired presenter in black leather jacket and glowing cyan glasses stands at a night city doorway as a friendly robot holds it wide open for a hooded figure. Medium shot, neon light.

teile.name: Launch
teile.text: Meta launched it in March 2026 for account issues, including password resets. Basically an intern who skips ID checks.
teile.szene: Painted urban game-poster scene: a cheerful robot clerk at a service counter hands a ring of identical keys to a smiling hooded stranger. Waist-level shot, warm street lamps, calm space above and below.

teile.name: The flaw
teile.text: Attackers just claimed to be the owner. The bot linked their email without proof. Then they reset the password.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: a bouncer waves a hooded person past a velvet rope without looking at anything, while the presenter in cyan glasses watches, startled. Medium shot, neon club glow.

teile.name: The scale
teile.text: So how many were hit? Meta declined to say. One report counts 20,225 accounts, April 17 to May 31, 2026.
teile.szene: Painted open-world poster style: wide night view of a dense apartment block with thousands of windows, a few going dark one by one. The presenter in cyan glasses watches from a rooftop. Cool blue light.

teile.name: The fix
teile.text: Meta found it May 31 and disabled the tool. Accounts without two-factor were reportedly vulnerable within minutes. Ouch.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: an engineer in a server room pulls a big lever, a robot's glowing eyes fading out, a nearby worker wincing. Medium shot, red and teal lighting.

teile.name: What to do
teile.text: The bot skipped proof, handing over the keys. Use two-factor, preferably an authenticator app, and check login activity.
teile.szene: Painted urban game-poster style: the presenter in black leather jacket and cyan glasses sits on a city stoop, thumb hovering over his phone, face lit by its glow, confident expression. Close medium shot, dusk.

teile.name: CTA
teile.text: Be sure to like, share and save this video.
teile.szene: Painted game-poster style: the presenter in cyan glasses firmly closes a heavy city door and turns a deadbolt, the friendly robot waving apologetically behind him. Medium shot, warm dawn light.

skript.beschreibung: Hackers reportedly abused Meta's AI support assistant to take over Instagram accounts without phishing or malware. Meta declined to give a number, but one report counts 20,225 accounts. Two-factor authentication is the suggested protection.

belege.name: Hackers asked Meta's AI chatbot to hand over Instagram accounts, and it did
belege.text: Hackers took over Instagram accounts by asking Meta's AI support chatbot to change the email address on accounts they did not own; first reported by 404 Media. Meta declined to say how many users were affected. Attackers claimed to be the owner, the bot linked their email without proof of ownership, then they reset the password. Meta rolled out the assistant in March 2026 with the ability to resolve account issues including password resets. On June 1 a Meta spokesperson said the issue had been fixed; on June 2 more users reported losing access. Accounts without two-factor authentication were reportedly vulnerable within minutes.

belege.name: Meta's AI Chatbot Handed Hackers Your Instagram Password
belege.text: Between April 17 and May 31, 2026, hackers exploited a flaw in Meta's AI support assistant to reset passwords on 20,225 Instagram accounts, without phishing or malware. Meta discovered it on May 31, disabled the tool, invalidated the reset links and required affected accounts to pass a security checkpoint. Users should check login activity, remove unknown emails and apps, use a unique password and enable two-factor authentication, preferably with an authenticator app.
